First, we reduce 173 modulo 50:
\[ 173 \div 50 = 3 \text{ remainder } 23, \]
so
\[ 173 \equiv 23 \pmod{50}. \]

Next, we reduce 927 modulo 50:
\[ 927 \div 50 = 18 \text{ remainder } 27, \]
so
\[ 927 \equiv 27 \pmod{50}. \]

Now we substitute these reduced values back into the original expression:
\[ 173 \cdot 927 \equiv 23 \cdot 27 \pmod{50}. \]

Next, we calculate \( 23 \cdot 27 \):
\[ 23 \cdot 27 = 621. \]

Now we reduce 621 modulo 50:
\[ 621 \div 50 = 12 \text{ remainder } 21, \]
so
\[ 621 \equiv 21 \pmod{50}. \]

Therefore, the value of \( n \) is
\[ \boxed{21}. \]
